````text
6: # Python Project Best Practice
7: 
8: An opinionated baseline for Python projects that both people and agents work
9: in. Two entry points: scaffold a new project (Workflow A), or score and
10: modernize an existing one (Workflow B). The same conventions drive both.
11: 
12: The bias throughout: **every operation has one canonical, discoverable,
13: non-interactive command**. That is what makes a project workable by an agent,
14: and it happens to be what makes it pleasant for humans.
15: 
16: ## When to use
17: 
18: - "Start a new Python project / package / CLI tool"
19: - "Set up pyproject.toml", "which should I use, uv or poetry / pip-tools?"
20: - "How do I make this installable so someone can just run it?"
21: - "Modernize this repo" — setup.py, requirements.txt, poetry, conda, flat layout
22: - Choosing between ruff/black, mypy/ty, extras/dependency-groups, just/taskipy
23: - Adding a CLI, notebooks, an HTTP surface, or a Rust extension to a Python repo
24: 
25: ## When NOT to use
26: 
27: These skills own their territory. Delegate rather than restate:
28: 
29: | Topic | Skill |
30: |---|---|
31: | `--help` / `--dry-run` / `--print-config` / exit-code design and verification | `verifiable-surfaces` |
32: | marimo dual-mode notebooks, sweeps, tracking | `marimo-batch-mlflow`; format rules in `marimo-notebook`; widgets in `anywidget` |
33: | Production FastAPI internals | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
34: | Docs site, GitHub Pages, llms.txt | `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` |
35: | Releasing a compiled Go/Rust binary | `cli-release-distribution` (Python distribution stays here) |

37: | TDD discipline itself | `engineering-fundamentals/tdd` |
38: | Building an MCP server | `mcp-builder` (read `references/api-and-services.md` first — usually you want a subcommand) |
39: 
40: Also not for: a one-file script (use a PEP 723 header and stop), or a
41: maintenance-only repo where a migration buys nothing.

43: ## Authoritative sources
44: 
45: Fetch the page rather than guessing — this toolchain moves fast, and several
46: of these projects change CLI surface between minor versions.
47: 
48: | Thing | Where |
49: |---|---|
50: | uv | <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/> · CLI reference <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/> |
51: | ruff rules | <https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/> |
52: | ty | <https://github.com/astral-sh/ty> (0.0.x — check the version before quoting behavior) |

56: | PyO3 / maturin | <https://pyo3.rs/> · <https://www.maturin.rs/> |

58: 
59: ## The canonical layout
60: 
61: ```
62: pyproject.toml          [project] + [dependency-groups] + tool config. One file.
63: uv.lock                 committed. Pins YOUR dev env, never your users'.
64: .python-version         dev interpreter (uv python pin). Not the same as requires-python.
65: Justfile                every supported operation. `just --list` is the surface.
66: AGENTS.md               the agent contract. CLAUDE.md is a symlink to it.
67: README.md               getting started for humans: uv sync, just check.
68: .envrc / .env.example   direnv activation; the tracked contract for .env (which is ignored).
69: 
70: src/my_tool/            src layout: tests import the INSTALLED package
71:   core.py               domain logic. stdlib logging. no side effects at import.
72:   _log.py               loguru setup. called by entry points only.
73:   settings.py           pydantic-settings: defaults < .env < environment.
74:   cli/                  one frozen dataclass per subcommand; run() -> exit code
75:   py.typed              without this your annotations are invisible to consumers
76: tests/                  mirrors src/ module for module
77: scripts/                repo helpers, NOT importable from the package
78: notebooks/              marimo notebooks. import the package; nothing imports them.
79: .agents/skills/my-tool/ the package's own skill, shipped with the code
80: .github/workflows/ci.yml  runs the same gate as `just check`
81: ```
82: 
83: Two arrows to keep straight: `notebooks/` and `scripts/` may import the
84: package; the package imports neither.
85: 
86: ## Decision: which profile?
87: 
88: Start at the smallest row that fits and add later — profiles are additive, so
89: "agentic later" costs nothing now.
90: 
91: | Profile | Use when | Adds | Read |
92: |---|---|---|---|
93: | `minimal` | a library nobody runs from a shell yet | package, tests, Justfile, CI, AGENTS.md | `uv-and-pyproject`, `quality-gates` |
94: | `cli` **(default)** | almost everything | Tyro CLI, loguru, pydantic-settings, `[project.scripts]` | + `tyro-cli`, `logging-and-config` |
95: | `lib` | others will import it | publishing metadata, `py.typed` | + `uv-and-pyproject` §Distribution |
96: | `api` | it serves HTTP | FastAPI app, `/docs`, `/openapi.json` | + `api-and-services` |
97: | `ml` | experiments and notebooks | marimo notebook that is also a CLI | + `notebooks-and-widgets` |
98: | `rust` | a profiled, CPU-bound hot loop | maturin backend, PyO3 crate, `.pyi` stubs | + `rust-pyo3` |
99: 
100: Companion skills to recommend, by profile, are in
101: [`references/agent-interface.md`](references/agent-interface.md) and in the
102: scaffolder's `recommended_skills[]`.

104: ## Workflow A — new project from zero
105: 
106: ### 1. Decide the profile and the name
107: 
108: Ask only what you cannot infer: what the project does, and whether it needs a
109: CLI, HTTP, notebooks, or Rust. The slug is hyphen-case (`churn-scorer`); the
110: package is the underscore form (`churn_scorer`). Everything else has a default.
111: 
112: ### 2. Generate
113: 
114: ```bash
115: # preview first — writes nothing
116: uv run skills/local/python-project-best-practice/scripts/new-python-project.py \
117:     --dry-run --profile cli ./my-tool
118: 
119: uv run .../new-python-project.py --profile cli --owner <gh-user> \
120:     --description "One line." ./my-tool
121: ```
122: 
123: JSON summary on stdout (`project`, `package`, `profile`, `files[]`,
124: `recommended_skills[]`, `next_steps[]`); progress on stderr.
125: 
126: ### 3. Verify it actually works
127: 
128: ```bash
129: cd ./my-tool
130: uv sync
131: just docs-sync     # fills the CLI block in AGENTS.md from --help
132: just check         # fmt + lint + types + tests + docs-drift
133: ```
134: 
135: `just check` must be green before you hand the project over. If it is not,
136: that is a bug in this skill's template — fix the template, not the generated
137: copy.
138: 
139: ### 4. Offer the companion skills
140: 
141: Print the install line and let the user choose:
142: 
143: ```bash
144: npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
145: ```
146: 
147: Do not vendor copies into the new repo — copies have no update path.

149: ## Workflow B — modernize an existing project
150: 
151: ### 1. Audit, read-only
152: 
153: ```bash
154: uv run skills/local/python-project-best-practice/scripts/audit-python-project.py \
155:     --format table /path/to/repo
156: ```
157: 
158: 26 checks with evidence and a fix hint, plus an ordered `migration_plan[]`.
159: Exit `4` when something fails. It never writes, and there is deliberately no
160: `--fix`.
161: 
162: ### 2. Show the user the plan and agree on scope
163: 
164: Nobody asked you to rewrite their build system. Confirm which rungs to do now.
165: 
166: ### 3. One rung per pull request
167: 
168: The ladder is ordered by dependency: environment → layout → dependency
169: declaration → lint/format → types → tests → task runner + CI → console script
170: → logging layering → agent contract → secrets. Each rung ends with the test
171: suite green.
172: 
173: Read [`references/legacy-refactor.md`](references/legacy-refactor.md) before
174: the first rung. The traps that ruin these migrations — `uv add -r
175: requirements.txt` flattening the dependency graph, a formatting commit
176: destroying `git blame`, a tracked `.env` needing rotation before any history
177: rewrite — are all there.
178: 
179: ## Available scripts
180: 
181: - **`scripts/new-python-project.py <target-dir>`** — scaffold from the bundled
182:   template tree. Offline; writes nothing outside the target.
183:   - Flags: `--profile {minimal,cli,lib,api,ml,rust}`, `--name`, `--description`,
184:     `--author`, `--owner`, `--python-floor`, `--python-pin`, `--dry-run`,
185:     `--force`, `--no-git`, `--help`.
186:   - Output: JSON on stdout, progress on stderr.
187:   - Exit: `0` ok · `2` usage · `3` target exists without `--force` ·
188:     `4` template tree and `assets/manifest.toml` disagree.
189: - **`scripts/audit-python-project.py [path]`** — read-only scorecard +
190:   migration plan.
191:   - Flags: `--format {json,table}`, `--fail-on {fail,warn,never}`, `--help`.
192:   - Exit: `0` clean · `3` path is not a directory · `4` findings at or above
193:     the threshold.
194: 
195: Both are PEP 723 `uv run` scripts with inline dependencies — no environment
196: setup needed before calling them.
197: 
198: ## Bundled assets
199: 
200: - `assets/project/` — the template tree. Every file ends `.tmpl`; the generator
201:   strips the suffix, substitutes placeholders, and drops
202:   `# __IF:profile,...__ … # __END__` blocks that the chosen profile does not
203:   want.
204: - `assets/manifest.toml` — maps each destination path to the profiles that get
205:   it. **A file not listed here is never copied**, and the generator fails
206:   (exit 4) if the manifest and the tree disagree in either direction.
207:

212: | File | Load when |

222: | [`legacy-refactor.md`](references/legacy-refactor.md) | Workflow B — reading the scorecard, ordering the migration |
223: 
224: ## Gotchas
225: 
226: - **`uv sync` deletes what is not in the lock.** A manual `uv pip install`
227:   disappears on the next sync with no warning. Change dependencies with
228:   `uv add` / `uv remove` so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` move together.
229: - **Do not run black and `ruff format` together.** `ruff format` is a black
230:   reimplementation; two formatters fight over magic trailing commas and quoting
231:   and every commit reformats the last one's output. Pick ruff.
232: - **A flat layout imports your source directory, not the installed package.**
233:   Missing `__init__.py`, missing `py.typed`, unshipped package data — all pass
234:   the test suite and break the user's install. `src/` is what closes that gap.
235: - **`[dependency-groups]` is not `[project.optional-dependencies]`.** An extra
236:   is published and installable by your users; a PEP 735 group is local-only.
237:   Your test runner in an extra is a defect you cannot remove without a release.
238:   `uv sync` installs the `dev` group by default.
239: - **`uv.lock` does not constrain your users.** Installed as a dependency, your
240:   package is resolved from `[project.dependencies]` and the lock is ignored.
241:   Commit it anyway — it pins your dev and CI environment, which is the point.
242: - **loguru in a library hijacks the importing program's logging.** Library
243:   modules use `logging.getLogger(__name__)`; only entry points call
244:   `_log.configure()`. Symptom: "my app's log format changed after I added a
245:   dependency."
246: - **`logger.add()` without `logger.remove()` prints everything twice.** loguru
247:   installs a default stderr sink at import. This is the most common loguru bug.
248: - **`diagnose=True` puts local variables in tracebacks** — a credential leak in
249:   production logs. Keep it off outside development.
250: - **`.python-version` is read by pyenv as well as uv.** A stale value silently
251:   changes which interpreter builds the venv. Write it with `uv python pin`.
252:   It is the dev pin; `requires-python` is the supported range. Keep both in CI.
253: - **`ruff`'s `target-version` should be your `requires-python` floor**, not
254:   your dev pin, or `UP` rewrites code to syntax your declared floor cannot run.
255: - **direnv cannot change `PS1`.** There is no `(.venv)` prompt even when the
256:   env is active — check `which python`, not the prompt. And `.envrc` needs
257:   `direnv allow` after every edit.
258: - **Tyro already has shell completion.** Do not add shtab, argcomplete, or a
259:   `completion` subcommand: `my-tool --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`.
260:   `--tyro-print-completion` is deprecated (a stray `print()` corrupts it), the
261:   bash completion filename must equal the command name, and no package manager
262:   installs completions for you.
263: - **No `[project.scripts]` means `uv tool install` gives the user no command.**
264:   `python -m pkg` is not a substitute for something on `PATH`.
265: - **marimo notebooks are real `.py` files**, so ruff lints them: without
266:   `per-file-ignores` for `notebooks/*` (`E402`, `F401`, `B018`) the gate fails
267:   and the formatter can reorder cell contents.
268: - **A PEP 723 script runs in its own environment.** A helper in `scripts/`
269:   with an inline header cannot `import your_package` unless the package is in
270:   its own `dependencies`.
271: - **`uv sync` does not rebuild a Rust extension after you edit `rust/`.** It
272:   sees the package as installed, does nothing, and you keep running the stale
273:   binary — including the print statements you just added to debug it. Use
274:   `uv sync --reinstall-package <slug>` or `maturin develop --uv`. A compiled
275:   module also needs a hand-written `.pyi`, or type checkers report
276:   `has no member`.
277: - **Never replace the `AGENTS.md`↔`CLAUDE.md` symlink with a real file.** Git
278:   stores it as mode `120000`; two real files drift and only one is right. A
279:   Windows checkout without symlink support materializes a text file containing
280:   the path — that is the corruption, not the fix.
281: - **Do not `uv add -r requirements.txt` when migrating.** A pip freeze is a
282:   flattened graph; that command promotes every transitive pin to a direct
283:   dependency. Add the packages you actually import and let the resolver work.
284: - **uv does not supply non-Python system libraries.** Some scientific stacks
285:   still need conda or OS packages. Say which ones in the README instead of
286:   pretending the migration is complete.
287: - **A tracked `.env` is an incident, not a cleanup.** Rotate every credential
288:   first; history rewriting is a later, separately-approved step. Hand off to
289:   `agent-history-hygiene`.
290:
````

````text
5: 
6: # Skill Author
7: 
8: Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9: https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10: every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11: once a draft exists).
12: 
13: ## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14: 
15: | Task | Use |
16: |---|---|
17: | "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18: | "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19: | "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20: | "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21: | "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22: | "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23: 
24: If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25: 
26: ## Workflow
27: 
28: ### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29: 
30: Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31: 
32: 1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33: 2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34: 3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35: 4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36: 
37: Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38: description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39: 
40: ### 2. Scaffold
41: 
42: Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43: auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44: symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45: 
46: ```bash
47: bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48: ```
49: 
50: Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51: 
52: | Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53: |---|---|---|
54: | **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55: | **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56: | **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57: 
58: The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59: purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60: 
61: > **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62: > but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63: > available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this

72: ### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73: 
74: Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75: that matter most:
76: 
77: - **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78:   descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79:   this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80:   501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81:   loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82: - **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83:   assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84: - **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85:   reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86: - **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87:   give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88: - **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89:   escape hatches.
90: 
91: Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92: `references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93: happens"), not just that it exists.
94: 
95: ### 4. Design any scripts
96: 
97: Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98: design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99: caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100: requirements:
101: 
102: - No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103: - `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104: - Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105: - Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106: - `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107: - Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108: 
109: For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110: `requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111: have to set up an environment first.
112: 
113: ### 5. Lint
114: 
115: Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116: 
117: ```bash
118: bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119: ```
120: 
121: It checks three things:
122: 
123: 1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124:    hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125:    respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126: 2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
127:    responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
128:    script).
129: 3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
130:    least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
131: 
132: Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.
133: 
134: ### 6. (Optional) Hand off to skill-creator
135: 
136: Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
137: quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
138: `skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure
139: right. If you want to validate it works on real prompts, the `skill-creator`
140: skill runs test cases and benchmarks."
141: 
142: ## Available scripts
143: 
144: - **`scripts/new-skill.sh <name>`** — Scaffold the canonical skill dir
145:   (SKILL.md, references/, scripts/, assets/) and add discovery symlinks for
146:   non-universal agents. Auto-detects scope (LOCAL / PROJECT / GLOBAL); see
147:   table in step 2.
148:   - Scope flags (mutually exclusive): `--local` (force this repo's
149:     `skills/local/`), `--project` (force `<repo>/.agents/skills/`),
150:     `--global` (force `~/.agents/skills/`).
151:   - Other flags: `--vendor` (LOCAL only — `skills/vendor/<name>/` instead of
152:     `skills/local/`; rare, vendored skills normally come via `vendor.yaml`);
153:     `--root DIR` (override walk-up); `--no-symlinks` (skip the fan-out);
154:     `--dry-run`; `--force` (overwrite existing canonical dir + replace
155:     symlinks).
156: - **`scripts/lint-skill.sh <skill-dir>`** — Run frontmatter, script hygiene,
157:   and reference reachability checks. Exit non-zero on any error.
158:   - Flags: `--strict` (treat warnings as errors); `--quiet` (only print failures).
159: - **`scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh [PATH...]`** — YAML-parse the frontmatter of
160:   every `SKILL.md` under PATH (default `.`) with a real parser, and check that
161:   the root is a mapping with string `name` + `description`. Catches the
162:   breakage class `lint-skill.sh`'s awk extractor cannot see — an unquoted
163:   `description:` containing `": "` makes `npx skills` (and Claude Code /
164:   Cursor) **silently skip the skill**. `lint-skill.sh` calls this for the
165:   single-skill case; run it directly to sweep a whole collection.
166:   - Flags: `--parser auto|yq|python3|node` (`node` = the js `yaml` package,
167:     exactly what `npx skills` uses); `--quiet`.
168: 
169: ## Bundled assets
170: 
171: Templates that `new-skill.sh` copies and that you can reference manually:
172: 
173: - `assets/SKILL.md.template` — Frontmatter + workflow skeleton with placeholders.
174: - `assets/reference.md.template` — Reference doc skeleton (TOC + sections).
175: - `assets/script-bash.template` — Bash 3.2 compatible script with `set -euo pipefail`,
176:   `--help` / `--dry-run` flag handler, structured-output friendly logging
177:   (data → stdout, prose → stderr).
178: - `assets/script-python.template` — Python script with PEP 723 inline-deps
179:   block, argparse with help/examples, dry-run support.
180: 
181: ## Reference files
182: 
183: - `references/authoring-patterns.md` — The agentskills.io "best practices"
184:   page condensed: gotchas, templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity,
185:   defaults-not-menus, procedures-over-declarations, plan-validate-execute.
186: - `references/script-design.md` — The agentskills.io "using scripts" page
187:   condensed: agentic CLI design, structured output, error message style,
188:   PEP 723, uvx/npx/pipx version pinning, dry-run patterns.
189: - `references/this-repo-conventions.md` — Conventions specific to *this*
190:   repository: where to put local vs vendor skills, how the 5-level skill
191:   search works, AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md sync, where mirrored scripts live.
192: 
193: ## Gotchas
194: 
195: - **AGENTS.md is a symlink to CLAUDE.md** — edit either one; never replace the
196:   symlink with a real file.
197: - **Skill discovery is one level deep first, then recursive up to 5 levels.**
198:   `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
199:   nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
200: - **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
201:   stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
202:   See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
203: - **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
204:   Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
205:   120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
206:   Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
207: - **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
208:   unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
209:   "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
210:   from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
211:   treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
212:   Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
213:   `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
214:   `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
215: - **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
216:   If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
217:   adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
218:   investing in authoring.
219: - **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
220:   a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
221:   `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
222:   a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
223:   it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
224:   explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
225:   system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
226: - **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
227:   POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
228:   script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
229:   if you ever hand-create one, see
230:   [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).
231: 
232: ## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
233: 
234: Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
235: identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
236: weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
237: check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
238: quantitative validation.
````

````text
1: # uv and pyproject.toml
2: 
3: Load this when writing or repairing `pyproject.toml`, deciding what goes in a
4: lockfile, choosing a build backend, pinning the interpreter, or publishing.
5: 
6: uv's CLI surface changes between minor versions. When you are unsure of a flag,
7: fetch <https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/cli/> rather than guessing.
8: 
9: ## The commands that matter
10: 
11: | Goal | Command |
12: |---|---|
13: | Start a project | `uv init --package --lib` (or `--app`) |
14: | Add a runtime dependency | `uv add httpx` |
15: | Add dev tooling | `uv add --dev pytest ruff` |
16: | Add to a named group | `uv add --group docs mkdocs-material` |
17: | Add a published extra | `uv add --optional postgres asyncpg` |
18: | Recreate the env from the lock | `uv sync` |
19: | Fail instead of re-resolving | `uv sync --locked` (use this in CI) |
20: | Check the lock is current | `uv lock --check` |
21: | Pin the interpreter | `uv python pin 3.13` |
22: | Run anything | `uv run <cmd>` |
23: | Bump the version | `uv version --bump minor` |
24: | Build + publish | `uv build && uv publish` |
25: 
26: `uv run` re-syncs before running. In a hot loop where you know the environment
27: is current, `uv run --no-sync` skips it.
28: 
29: ## Groups vs extras
30: 
31: This is the distinction people get wrong, and getting it wrong ships your test
32: runner to your users.
33: 
34: ```toml
35: [project.optional-dependencies]   # PUBLISHED. `pip install yourpkg[postgres]`
36: postgres = ["asyncpg>=0.30"]
37: 
38: [dependency-groups]               # LOCAL ONLY. PEP 735. Never published.
39: dev = ["pytest>=8.3", "ruff>=0.9"]
40: docs = ["mkdocs-material>=9.5"]
41: ```
42: 
43: `dev` is special-cased: `uv sync` and `uv run` include it by default. Other
44: groups need `--group docs`. `--no-default-groups` gives a runtime-only env.
45: 
46: A dev tool in `optional-dependencies` is a real defect: it appears in your
47: package metadata, resolves into your users' dependency graph if they ever
48: install the extra, and cannot be removed without a release.
49: 
50: > Interop note: some tooling still generates a `docs` **extra** — for example
51: > the `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill writes `[project.optional-dependencies]
52: > docs`. That keeps working (`uv sync --extra docs`); it is not worth a
53: > migration unless you are publishing the package.
54: 
55: ## Lockfile policy
56: 
57: Commit `uv.lock`. For applications and CLIs this is obvious. For libraries it
58: is also right, and the usual objection is based on a misunderstanding:
59: 
60: **`uv.lock` never constrains your users.** When someone installs your package
61: as a dependency, their resolver reads `[project.dependencies]` and ignores your
62: lock entirely. The lock pins *your* development and CI environment, which is
63: exactly what you want reproducible.
64: 
65: What the lock does not do is prove your declared ranges are honest. If you
66: support `>=3.11` and a floor of `httpx>=0.28`, add a CI job that resolves
67: against the lowest versions (`uv sync --resolution lowest-direct`), otherwise
68: your floors are aspirational.
69: 
70: ## Interpreter pinning
71: 
72: `.python-version` holds the development interpreter. `uv python pin 3.13`
73: writes it, and `uv sync` downloads that interpreter if it is missing — no
74: system Python of that version required.
75: 
76: `requires-python` in `[project]` is a different thing: the *range you support*.
77: Keep the floor lower than the pin, and put both ends in the CI matrix. The two
78: drift apart silently otherwise.
79: 
80: `.python-version` is also read by pyenv. On a machine with both, a stale value
81: changes which interpreter builds the venv, with no warning.
82: 
83: ## Build backends
84: 
85: | Backend | When |
86: |---|---|
87: | `hatchling` | default. Plugin ecosystem (`hatch-vcs` for git-tag versions) |
88: | `uv_build` | lean, fast, no plugins. Fine for a pure-Python package |
89: | `maturin` | any Rust/PyO3 extension |
90: | `scikit-build-core` | C/C++/CMake extensions |
91: 
92: With a src layout and a hyphenated project name, name the package directory
93: explicitly so the backend does not have to guess:
94: 
95: ```toml
96: [tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
97: packages = ["src/my_tool"]
98: ```
99: 
100: ## Distribution
101: 
102: Tier 0, and enough for most internal tools — no PyPI account needed:
103: 
104: ```bash
105: uv tool install git+https://github.com/owner/repo@v0.1.0
106: uvx --from git+https://github.com/owner/repo my-tool --help   # run once
107: ```
108: 
109: Both require `[project.scripts]`. A package that can only be run as
110: `python -m pkg` gives the installer no command on `PATH`.
111: 
112: For PyPI, use Trusted Publishing (OIDC): configure the publisher on PyPI for
113: `owner/repo` + workflow filename, then give the job `id-token: write`. No API
114: token in Actions secrets, nothing to rotate or leak.
115: 
116: ```yaml
117: permissions:
118:   id-token: write
119: steps:
120:   - run: uv build
121:   - run: uv publish        # picks up the OIDC token automatically
122: ```
123: 
124: ## Workspaces
125: 
126: For a monorepo of related packages, one lockfile and one venv for all of them:
127: 
128: ```toml
129: [tool.uv.workspace]
130: members = ["packages/*"]
131: 
132: [tool.uv.sources]
133: my-core = { workspace = true }
134: ```
135: 
136: Members share the resolution, so a version conflict between two members is a
137: hard error rather than two silently different environments. If the packages
138: genuinely need different dependency versions, they are not a workspace.
````

````text
1: # Quality gates: ruff, types, pytest, CI
2: 
3: Load this when configuring lint/format/type/test tooling, setting up CI, or
4: deciding what `just check` should contain.
5: 
6: ## One gate, four rungs
7: 
8: `just check` = `fmt-check` → `lint-check` → `types` → `test` → `docs-check`,
9: ordered so the cheapest failure comes first. CI runs the same commands. If a
10: check exists only in CI, contributors discover it after pushing; if it exists
11: only locally, it stops being true.
12: 
13: ## ruff does lint AND format
14: 
15: ```toml
16: [tool.ruff]
17: line-length = 100
18: target-version = "py311"
19: src = ["src", "tests"]
20: 
21: [tool.ruff.lint]
22: select = ["E", "W", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "C4", "RUF"]
23: ```
24: 
25: - `I` replaces isort, `UP` modernizes syntax to your `target-version`, `B`
26:   catches real bugs (mutable defaults, loop-variable capture), `SIM` and `C4`
27:   simplify, `RUF` is ruff's own set.
28: - **Do not also install black.** `ruff format` is a reimplementation of black's
29:   algorithm; running both means two tools rewriting the same file, disagreeing
30:   over magic trailing commas and string quoting. Pick ruff.
31: - `target-version` should equal your `requires-python` floor, not your
32:   development pin. `UP` rewrites to the *lowest* version you claim to support.
33: 
34: Per-file ignores earn their keep in exactly two places:
35: 
36: ```toml
37: [tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
38: "notebooks/*" = ["E402", "F401", "B018"]   # marimo cells are not linear scripts
39: "tests/*" = ["S101"]                        # only if you enable flake8-bandit
40: ```
41: 
42: ## Type checking
43: 
44: Two defensible defaults:
45: 
46: | | `ty` | `mypy` |
47: |---|---|---|
48: | Speed | very fast (Rust, incremental) | slow on large trees |
49: | Maturity | **0.0.x, pre-1.0** — diagnostics change between patch releases | stable, a decade of edge cases |
50: | Editor | ships a language server | via pylsp/pyright |
51: 
52: The template defaults to `ty` and pins it, because a type checker that reruns
53: in under a second is one people actually run. Pin it *exactly* — `ty==0.0.74`,
54: not `>=` — or a routine `uv lock --upgrade` will change what your gate accepts.
55: 
56: Switch to mypy by replacing the dev dependency and the `just types` recipe:
57: 
58: ```toml
59: [tool.mypy]
60: strict = true
61: files = ["src", "tests"]
62: ```
63: 
64: Whichever you pick: ship `py.typed` in the package. Without that marker, a
65: consumer's type checker ignores every annotation you wrote.
66: 
67: Compiled extensions are invisible to both. A PyO3 module needs a hand-written
68: `.pyi` next to it or the checker reports `has no member`; see
69: [`rust-pyo3.md`](rust-pyo3.md).
70: 
71: ## pytest layout
72: 
73: ```
74: src/my_tool/core.py
75: tests/test_core.py        # mirrors src/, module for module
76: ```
77: 
78: Tests live outside `src/`. With a src layout, `uv run pytest` imports the
79: *installed* package, so a missing `__init__.py`, a missing `py.typed`, or
80: un-shipped package data fails in your test run instead of in a user's install.
81: A flat layout imports the working directory and hides all three.
82: 
83: ```toml
84: [tool.pytest.ini_options]
85: addopts = "-q --strict-markers --strict-config"
86: testpaths = ["tests"]
87: ```
88: 
89: Keep coverage out of `addopts`. Always-on coverage slows every run, breaks
90: debugger attach, and trains people to ignore the number. Put it in one recipe
91: and in CI:
92: 
93: ```bash
94: uv run pytest --cov --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80
95: ```
96: 
97: ## TDD, and why it is the loop that works with agents
98: 
99: Write the failing test first, then the code that passes it. With an agent in
100: the loop this stops being a style preference: the test is the only part of the
101: exchange that is machine-checkable. "Make the tests pass" is a verifiable
102: instruction; "implement the feature" is not.
103: 
104: Practical shape:
105: 
106: 1. Write the test. Run it. **Confirm it fails, and for the stated reason** — a
107:    test that passes before the implementation exists is testing nothing.
108: 2. Implement the smallest change that passes it.
109: 3. `just check`.
110: 4. Refactor with the gate green.
111: 
112: For the discipline itself — how to pick the next test, when to stub, how to
113: avoid tests that encode the implementation — use the vendored
114: `engineering-fundamentals/tdd` skill. This section only covers the mechanics.
115: 
116: ## CI
117: 
118: ```yaml
119: - uses: actions/checkout@v5
120: - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v10
121:   with:
122:     enable-cache: true
123:     python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
124: - run: uv sync --locked        # fails on a stale lock instead of re-resolving
125: - run: uv run ruff format --check .
126: - run: uv run ruff check .
127: - run: uv run ty check
128: - run: uv run pytest --cov --cov-fail-under=80
129: ```
130: 
131: Notes worth the line each:
132: 
133: - `--locked`, not plain `uv sync`. Without it, CI silently resolves a different
134:   dependency set than your machine and the lockfile stops meaning anything.
135: - Matrix the `requires-python` floor and the `.python-version` pin. Testing
136:   only the pin means your declared floor is untested.
137: - Pin actions to a release tag, or a commit SHA if you want supply-chain
138:   hardening. `@master` is a remote-code-execution surface you do not control.
139: - Action majors move. Check the current one rather than copying an old
140:   workflow — `setup-uv` was on v6 not long ago.
141: 
142: ## pre-commit
143: 
144: Useful for the fast rungs (format, lint, secret detection) so bad commits never
145: land. Do not duplicate the whole gate there — a pre-commit hook that runs the
146: test suite gets bypassed with `-n` within a week.
147: 
148: The `agent-history-hygiene` skill already bootstraps pre-commit with secret
149: scanning; add ruff hooks to that config rather than starting a second one.
````

```text
119: def load_manifest() -> dict[str, str]:
120:     with MANIFEST.open("rb") as handle:
121:         return tomllib.load(handle)["files"]
122: 
123: 
124: def check_manifest(files: dict[str, str]) -> None:
125:     """Fail loudly when the manifest and the template tree disagree."""
126:     on_disk = {
127:         str(path.relative_to(TEMPLATE_DIR))[: -len(".tmpl")]
128:         for path in TEMPLATE_DIR.rglob("*.tmpl")
129:     }
130:     listed = set(files)
131:     if missing := sorted(listed - on_disk):
132:         die(
133:             "assets/manifest.toml lists files that do not exist: "
134:             + ", ".join(missing)
135:             + " (expected each as assets/project/<path>.tmpl)",
136:             4,
137:         )
138:     if unlisted := sorted(on_disk - listed):
139:         die(
140:             "template files are not listed in assets/manifest.toml: "
141:             + ", ".join(unlisted)
142:             + " (an unlisted file is never copied - add it to [files])",
143:             4,
144:         )
145: 
146: 
147: def wanted(spec: str, profile: str) -> bool:
148:     return spec.strip() == "*" or profile in spec.split()
149: 
150: 
151: def apply_markers(text: str, profile: str) -> str:
152:     """Drop `# __IF:a,b__ ... # __END__` blocks that this profile does not want.
153: 
154:     Marker lines are always removed; only the body between them is conditional.
155:     """
156:     out: list[str] = []
157:     keep_stack: list[bool] = []
158:     # After a block is dropped, its surrounding blank lines would double up.
159:     # Squeeze only those. Never touch blank lines elsewhere: two blank lines
160:     # between top-level defs is required formatting, not slack.
161:     squeeze = False
162:     for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
163:         if match := _IF.match(line):
164:             names = [name.strip() for name in match.group(1).split(",") if name.strip()]
165:             keep_stack.append(profile in names)
166:             continue
167:         if _END.match(line):
168:             if not keep_stack:
169:                 die("unbalanced __END__ marker in template", 4)
170:             squeeze = not keep_stack.pop()
171:             continue
172:         if not all(keep_stack):
173:             continue
174:         if squeeze and not line.strip():
175:             if out and not out[-1].strip():
176:                 continue
177:         squeeze = False
178:         out.append(line)
179:     if keep_stack:
180:         die("unclosed __IF__ marker in template", 4)
181:     return "".join(out)
182: 
183: 
184: def substitutions(args: Args, slug: str, package: str) -> dict[str, str]:
185:     description = args.description.strip()
186:     if description and not description.endswith((".", "!", "?")):
187:         description += "."
188:     return {
189:         "PROJECT_SLUG_PLACEHOLDER": slug,
190:         "PACKAGE_NAME_PLACEHOLDER": package,
191:         "PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER": description,
192:         "AUTHOR_PLACEHOLDER": args.author,
193:         "OWNER_PLACEHOLDER": args.owner,
194:         "PYTHON_FLOOR_PLACEHOLDER": args.python_floor,
195:         "PYTHON_PIN_PLACEHOLDER": args.python_pin,
196:         "RUFF_TARGET_PLACEHOLDER": "py" + args.python_floor.replace(".", ""),
197:         "ABI3_PLACEHOLDER": args.python_floor.replace(".", ""),
198:         "ENV_PREFIX_PLACEHOLDER": package.upper() + "_",
199:     }
200: 
201: 
202: def render(text: str, subs: dict[str, str], *, yaml_safe: bool) -> str:
203:     for token, value in subs.items():
204:         if yaml_safe and token == "PROJECT_DESCRIPTION_PLACEHOLDER":
205:             # The self-skill embeds this inside a single-quoted YAML scalar.
206:             value = value.replace("'", "''")
207:         text = text.replace(token, value)
208:     return text
209: 
210: 
211: def destination(rel: str, slug: str, package: str) -> Path:
212:     parts = [package if part == "PACKAGE" else slug if part == "SLUG" else part
213:              for part in Path(rel).parts]
214:     return Path(*parts)
215: 
216: 
217: def main(args: Args) -> None:
218:     if args.profile not in PROFILES:
219:         die(f"unknown profile {args.profile!r}; choose one of {', '.join(PROFILES)}", 2)
220: 
221:     target = Path(args.target).expanduser().resolve()
222:     slug = (args.name or target.name).strip().lower()
223:     if not _SLUG_OK.match(slug):
224:         die(
225:             f"invalid project name {slug!r}: use lower-case hyphen-separated words "
226:             "(e.g. churn-scorer). Pass --name to override the directory basename.",
227:             2,
228:         )
229:     package = slug.replace("-", "_")
230: 
231:     if target.exists() and any(target.iterdir()) and not args.force and not args.dry_run:
232:         die(f"{target} exists and is not empty; pass --force to overwrite", 3)
233: 
234:     files = load_manifest()
235:     check_manifest(files)
236:     subs = substitutions(args, slug, package)
237: 
238:     written: list[str] = []
239:     for rel, spec in sorted(files.items()):
240:         if not wanted(spec, args.profile):
241:             continue
242:         source = TEMPLATE_DIR / (rel + ".tmpl")
243:         rel_out = destination(rel, slug, package)
244:         body = apply_markers(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), args.profile)
245:         body = render(body, subs, yaml_safe=rel.startswith(".agents/skills/"))
246:         written.append(str(rel_out))
247:         if args.dry_run:
248:             continue
249:         out = target / rel_out
250:         out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
251:         out.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
252:         if rel.startswith("scripts/") and rel.endswith(".py"):
253:             out.chmod(0o755)
254: 
255:     # CLAUDE.md is a symlink so both agent conventions read one file.
256:     symlink = "CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md"
257:     if not args.dry_run:
258:         link = target / "CLAUDE.md"
259:         if link.is_symlink() or link.exists():
260:             link.unlink()
261:         link.symlink_to("AGENTS.md")

268:             capture_output=True,
269:             text=True,

272:         git_initialised = result.returncode == 0
273:         if not git_initialised:
274:             log(f"warning: git init failed: {result.stderr.strip()}")
275: 
276:     extras = {

280:         "api": ["verifiable-surfaces", "fastapi-ai-patterns"],

282:                "marimo-batch-mlflow"],

284:     }[args.profile]

286:     next_steps = [

289:         "just check",
```

```text
268:         "discoverable command surface for humans and agents")
269: 
270:     workflows = list((root / ".github" / "workflows").glob("*.y*ml"))
271:     add("ci-workflow", "pass" if workflows else "warn",
272:         f"{len(workflows)} workflow(s)" if workflows else "no GitHub Actions workflows",
273:         "" if workflows else "add .github/workflows/ci.yml running the same gate as `just check`")
274: 
275:     floating = []
276:     for workflow in workflows:
277:         for line in workflow.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
278:             if match := re.search(r"uses:\s*([\w./-]+)@(\S+)", line):
279:                 if match.group(2) in {"main", "master", "latest"}:
280:                     floating.append(f"{workflow.name}: {match.group(0).strip()}")
281:     add("ci-pinned-actions", "warn" if floating else "pass",
282:         "; ".join(floating) if floating else "no floating action refs",
283:         "pin actions to a release tag or commit SHA" if floating else "")
284: 
285:     # --- logging layering ----------------------------------------------------
286:     offenders = []
287:     for package in packages:
288:         for module in package.rglob("*.py"):
289:             rel = module.relative_to(root)
290:             if any(part in {"cli", "api", "__main__.py"} for part in rel.parts):
291:                 continue
292:             if module.name in {"_log.py", "log.py", "logging_setup.py"}:
293:                 continue
294:             body = module.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
295:             if re.search(r"^\s*from loguru import|^\s*import loguru", body, re.M):
296:                 offenders.append(str(rel))
297:     if not packages:
298:         add("loguru-layering", "n/a", "no package to check", "")
299:     else:
300:         add("loguru-layering", "warn" if offenders else "pass",
301:             f"loguru imported in library modules: {', '.join(offenders[:5])}"
302:             if offenders else "loguru confined to entry points",
303:             "library modules use logging.getLogger(__name__); only entry points call "
304:             "loguru's add()/remove(). A library that configures loguru hijacks the logging "
305:             "of every program that imports it" if offenders else "")
306: 
307:     # --- agent contract ------------------------------------------------------
308:     agents, claude = root / "AGENTS.md", root / "CLAUDE.md"
309:     add("agents-md", "pass" if (agents.exists() or claude.exists()) else "warn",
310:         "AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md present" if (agents.exists() or claude.exists())
311:         else "neither AGENTS.md nor CLAUDE.md",
312:         "" if (agents.exists() or claude.exists()) else
313:         "write AGENTS.md: commands, layout, conventions, and a CLI reference block")
314: 
315:     if agents.exists() and claude.exists():
316:         linked = agents.is_symlink() or claude.is_symlink()
317:         add("agents-md-symlink", "pass" if linked else "warn",
318:             "one file, one symlink" if linked else "AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are both real files",
319:             "" if linked else
320:             "ln -sf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md - two real files drift, and only one of them "
321:             "will be right")
322:     else:
323:         add("agents-md-symlink", "n/a", "only one of the two exists", "")
324: 
325:     # --- secrets -------------------------------------------------------------
326:     tracked_env = git_tracked(root, ".env")
327:     add("env-not-tracked", "fail" if tracked_env else "pass",
328:         ".env is tracked by git" if tracked_env else ".env not tracked",
329:         "git rm --cached .env, add it to .gitignore, ROTATE every credential it held, "
330:         "and only then consider rewriting history" if tracked_env else "")
331: 
332:     ignore = (root / ".gitignore").read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") \
333:         if (root / ".gitignore").exists() else ""
334:     missing = [entry for entry in (".venv", ".env") if entry not in ignore]
335:     add("gitignore-basics", "warn" if missing else "pass",
336:         f"not ignored: {', '.join(missing)}" if missing else ".venv and .env ignored",
337:         f"add {' and '.join(missing)} to .gitignore" if missing else "")
338: 
339:     return checks
340: 
341: 
342: def plan(checks: list[Check]) -> list[dict]:
343:     by_id = {check.id: check for check in checks}
344:     steps = []
345:     for title, ids in RUNGS:
346:         outstanding = [i for i in ids if i in by_id and by_id[i].status in {"warn", "fail"}]
347:         if outstanding:
348:             steps.append({"step": len(steps) + 1, "action": title, "resolves": outstanding})
349:     return steps
350: 
351: 
352: def render_table(checks: list[Check], steps: list[dict]) -> str:
353:     mark = {"pass": "ok  ", "warn": "WARN", "fail": "FAIL", "n/a": "-   "}
354:     width = max(len(check.id) for check in checks)
355:     lines = [f"{mark[c.status]}  {c.id.ljust(width)}  {c.evidence}" for c in checks]
356:     if steps:
357:         lines.append("")
358:         lines.append("Migration plan (one rung per pull request):")
359:         for step in steps:
360:             lines.append(f"  {step['step']}. {step['action']}")
361:             lines.append(f"     resolves: {', '.join(step['resolves'])}")
362:     return "\n".join(lines)
363: 
364: 
365: @dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)
366: class Args:
367:     """Score a Python project against modern-project conventions. Read-only."""
368: 
369:     path: tyro.conf.Positional[str] = "."
370:     """Project root to audit."""
371: 
372:     format: Literal["json", "table"] = "json"
373:     """json for machines, table for humans."""
374: 
375:     fail_on: Literal["fail", "warn", "never"] = "fail"
376:     """Lowest status that makes this exit non-zero."""
377: 
378: 
379: def main(args: Args) -> None:
380:     root = Path(args.path).expanduser().resolve()
381:     if not root.is_dir():
382:         print(f"error: {root} is not a directory", file=sys.stderr)
383:         raise SystemExit(3)
384: 
385:     checks = audit(root)
386:     steps = plan(checks)
387:     counts = {status: sum(1 for c in checks if c.status == status)
388:               for status in ("pass", "warn", "fail", "n/a")}
389: 
390:     if args.format == "table":
391:         print(render_table(checks, steps))
392:     else:
393:         print(json.dumps({
394:             "path": str(root),
395:             "summary": counts,
396:             "checks": [dataclasses.asdict(check) for check in checks],
397:             "migration_plan": steps,
398:         }, indent=2))
399: 
400:     print(
401:         f"{counts['pass']} pass, {counts['warn']} warn, {counts['fail']} fail "
402:         f"({counts['n/a']} n/a)",
403:         file=sys.stderr,
404:     )
405:     threshold = {"fail": 2, "warn": 1, "never": 99}[args.fail_on]
406:     if any(RANK[check.status] >= threshold for check in checks):
407:         raise SystemExit(4)
408: 
409: 
410: if __name__ == "__main__":
411:     os.environ.setdefault("COLUMNS", "100")
412:     try:
413:         main(tyro.cli(Args, prog="audit-python-project.py", description=__doc__))
414:     except SystemExit:
415:         raise
416:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - top-level guard, message is the contract
417:         print(f"error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
418:         raise SystemExit(1) from exc
```

````text
1: # Modernizing an existing project
2: 
3: Load this for Workflow B: an existing repo that needs to reach the conventions
4: in this skill, and reading the audit scorecard.
5: 
6: ## Rules of engagement
7: 
8: 1. **The audit is read-only, and so is the first conversation.** Run
9:    `audit-python-project.py --format table`, show the user, agree on scope.
10:    Nobody asked you to rewrite their build system.
11: 2. **One rung per pull request.** The migration plan is ordered because each
12:    rung depends on the ones above it. A single "modernize tooling" PR touching
13:    layout, packaging, lint, and CI at once cannot be reviewed, cannot be
14:    bisected, and will be reverted wholesale when something breaks.
15: 3. **The test suite is the safety net; if there isn't one, that is the first
16:    rung with real content.** Migrating layout and packaging without tests is
17:    moving furniture in the dark.
18: 4. **Do not "fix" warnings the user did not ask about.** Report them and move
19:    on.
20: 
21: ## Reading the scorecard
22: 
23: | Status | Meaning |
24: |---|---|
25: | `fail` | actively causes wrong behavior or blocks the rest of the ladder |
26: | `warn` | legacy or missing, but nothing is broken today |
27: | `n/a` | not applicable to this project shape |
28: 
29: `--fail-on warn` makes the audit a CI gate once the project is clean. Exit code
30: `4` means something at or above the threshold.
31: 
32: The `migration_plan` array omits rungs with nothing outstanding, so a partially
33: modern project gets a short plan rather than the whole ladder.
34: 
35: ## The ladder
36: 
37: ### 1. uv as the single source of truth
38: 
39: Get `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock` + `.python-version` in place first; everything
40: else depends on being able to reproduce the environment.
41: 
42: **Do not `uv add -r requirements.txt`.** A pip freeze is a flattened graph:
43: that command promotes every transitive pin to a direct dependency, and you
44: inherit a hundred constraints you did not choose and cannot upgrade. Instead:
45: 
46: ```bash
47: uv init --package                 # or hand-write [project] in pyproject.toml
48: uv add <the packages you import>  # imports only; let the resolver do the rest
49: uv lock && uv sync
50: uv run pytest                     # then reconcile what actually broke
51: ```
52: 
53: Read the imports, not the file. `grep -rhoE '^(from|import) [a-z_]+' src/ |
54: sort -u` is a faster first pass than reading `requirements.txt`.
55: 
56: From poetry: convert `[tool.poetry]` to a PEP 621 `[project]` table first, then
57: uv takes over. From conda: port everything that is a Python package, and keep
58: conda only for system libraries uv genuinely cannot supply (some CUDA, GDAL,
59: proprietary solvers). Say which ones in the README.
60: 
61: Keep `setup.py` until the wheel builds and installs identically, then delete it
62: in its own commit.
63: 
64: ### 2. src layout
65: 
66: ```bash
67: git mv oldpkg src/oldpkg
68: ```
69: 
70: Then `uv sync && uv run pytest` and expect failures — that is the point.
71: Anything that breaks here was previously passing only because the working
72: directory was on `sys.path`: missing `__init__.py`, package data referenced by
73: relative path, a test importing a module that was never packaged. Every one of
74: those was already broken for anyone installing your wheel.
75: 
76: ### 3–7. Dependency groups, ruff, types, tests, task runner + CI
77: 
78: Mechanical; see [`quality-gates.md`](quality-gates.md). Two sequencing notes:
79: 
80: - Land `ruff format` as a **separate, formatting-only commit** with no logic
81:   changes, and record its SHA in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`. Otherwise you lose
82:   `git blame` across the whole codebase.
83: - Turn `select` rules on in batches, not all at once. `["E", "F", "I"]` first,
84:   fix, commit; then `["UP", "B"]`; then the rest. A 4,000-violation first run
85:   gets `--fix --unsafe-fixes`'d in frustration and reviewed by nobody.
86: - If you drop black for `ruff format`, remove black in the same commit. Two
87:   formatters is worse than either.
88: 
89: ### 8. Console script
90: 
91: If the project has a CLI module but no `[project.scripts]`, users have no
92: command after install. Adding the entry point is usually three lines and the
93: highest-visibility change on this list.
94: 
95: ### 9. Logging layering
96: 
97: The audit flags `loguru` imported outside entry points. The fix is
98: mechanical — swap those modules to `logging.getLogger(__name__)` and move the
99: `logger.add()` call into `_log.configure()` — but it changes log output, so do
100: it alone and eyeball the result. See [`logging-and-config.md`](logging-and-config.md).
101: 
102: ### 10. Agent contract
103: 
104: `AGENTS.md` + the symlink + the package's own skill. See
105: [`agent-interface.md`](agent-interface.md).
106: 
107: ### 11. Secrets
108: 
109: `env-not-tracked` is the only check that can mean an active incident. If `.env`
110: is tracked, the order is **rotate first, rewrite later**:
111: 
112: 1. Rotate every credential in that file. The history is already on every clone,
113:    every fork, and every CI cache; a force-push does not un-leak it.
114: 2. `git rm --cached .env`, add it to `.gitignore`, commit.
115: 3. Only then discuss history rewriting, and only with the user's explicit
116:    go-ahead — it breaks every open PR and every existing clone.
117: 
118: The `agent-history-hygiene` skill owns this remediation path, including
119: pre-commit secret scanning so it does not recur. Hand off to it.
120: 
121: ## What not to migrate
122: 
123: - A project in maintenance with no active development. The migration has a
124:   cost and no payoff.
125: - Notebooks with published output that people cite. Convert new work to marimo;
126:   leave the archive alone.
127: - A conda environment that exists because of non-Python system libraries. uv
128:   does not replace that, and pretending otherwise breaks the build on someone
129:   else's machine.
````

````text
6: ## Ground rules

50: - **Logging.** `core.py` and every other library module use

52:   call `_log.configure()`. A library that calls `loguru.logger.add()` hijacks
````

````text
1: # The agent interface: AGENTS.md, the self-skill, and the drift gate
2: 
3: Load this when writing AGENTS.md, adding the package's own skill, or wiring the
4: check that stops those docs from going stale.
5: 
6: ## Three artifacts, three audiences
7: 
8: | File | Audience | Answers |
9: |---|---|---|
10: | `README.md` | a human evaluating or installing | what is this, how do I install and run it |
11: | `AGENTS.md` | an agent working *in* this repo | how do I change this code correctly |
12: | `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | an agent *using* the tool elsewhere | how do I drive this CLI |
13: 
14: They overlap in content and differ in purpose. Do not merge them: the README
15: gets read by someone deciding whether to try the tool, AGENTS.md by something
16: about to edit it.
17: 
18: ## AGENTS.md ↔ CLAUDE.md
19: 
20: Write one real file and symlink the other:
21: 
22: ```bash
23: ln -sf AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md
24: ```
25: 
26: `AGENTS.md` is the cross-agent convention (Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Claude Code
27: all read it or its symlink), so make that the real file. The direction is
28: arbitrary as long as exactly one is a symlink — *this* skills repo happens to
29: use the reverse.
30: 
31: Never replace the symlink with a real file. Git stores it as mode `120000`;
32: two real files drift within a week and only one of them will be right. On a
33: Windows checkout without symlink support the link materializes as a text file
34: containing the path `AGENTS.md`, which looks like corruption — that is what it
35: is, and re-creating the symlink fixes it.
36: 
37: ## What belongs in AGENTS.md
38: 
39: Only things an agent would otherwise get wrong. Not a tutorial.
40: 
41: - **The command surface.** "Use `just`; `just --list` is complete." An agent
42:   that has to infer commands from CI config will infer them wrong.
43: - **Prohibitions with reasons.** "Never `pip install` — `uv sync` erases it."
44:   A rule without a reason gets rationalized away.
45: - **Layout, one line per directory**, including which direction imports flow.
46: - **Non-obvious conventions.** Where logging is configured and why library
47:   modules must not; the exit-code contract; where a new setting has to be
48:   added (`settings.py` *and* `.env.example`).
49: - **The definition of done.** `just check` passes.
50: 
51: Leave out anything the code already states plainly. Every line costs context on
52: every request.
53: 
54: ## The package's own skill
55: 
56: Ship `.agents/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` inside the repo. Two payoffs: agents
57: working in *this* repo pick it up from the filesystem, and downstream users get
58: it in the same install as the code — the tool and its instructions version
59: together, so an agent never reads last release's flags.
60: 
61: It should carry what a caller needs and nothing more: install line, exit-code
62: table, the stdout/stderr split, how to add a subcommand, and the generated CLI
63: reference.
64: 
65: Frontmatter `description` is always-on context for every agent that loads the
66: skill. Make it name concrete trigger situations, keep it in the 120–500
67: character range, and **quote it** if it contains `:` or `#` — an unquoted YAML
68: scalar containing `": "` makes loaders drop the skill silently. See the
69: `skill-author` skill for the full authoring rules.
70: 
71: ## The drift gate
72: 
73: Prose about a CLI rots the first time someone renames a flag. Generate it
74: instead:
75: 
76: ```bash
77: just docs-sync     # rewrite the block between the CLI markers from --help
78: just docs-check    # exit 1 if the committed block is stale  (part of `just check`)
79: ```
80: 
81: `scripts/sync_agent_docs.py` runs `python -m <pkg>.cli --help` plus each
82: subcommand's `--help`, strips ANSI, and splices the result between
83: `<!-- BEGIN CLI -->` and `<!-- END CLI -->` in every target file. Because
84: `--check` is in `just check` and in CI, a flag rename that skips the docs fails
85: the build. The docs become a build artifact with a test, rather than prose
86: someone has to remember.
87: 
88: Two details that make it deterministic: force `NO_COLOR=1` and a fixed
89: `COLUMNS`, or the block churns depending on whose terminal ran it.
90: 
91: ## Recommended companion skills
92: 
93: Print these in the scaffolder's `next_steps[]` and list them in AGENTS.md.
94: Do not vendor copies into the project — copies go stale and there is no update
95: path. One install line covers all of them:
96: 
97: ```bash
98: npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills
99: ```
100: 
101: | Always | Why |
102: |---|---|
103: | `project-knowledge-harness` | `TODO.md` / `backlog/` / `pitfalls/` so deferred work and past traps survive the session |
104: | `agent-history-hygiene` | commit agent transcripts and plans with the diff, without leaking `.env` |
105: | `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` | GitHub Pages docs for humans, `llms.txt` for agents |
106: | `verifiable-surfaces` | the `--help` / `--dry-run` / exit-code discipline this layout assumes |
107: | `git-workflow` | Conventional Commits and AI-provenance trailers |
108: 
109: | By project type | |
110: |---|---|
111: | ML | `mlflow-tracking`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `experiment-knowledge-harness`, `marimo-batch-mlflow` |
112: | HTTP service | `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold` |
113: | Library for others | `cli-release-distribution` (its Python section is `uv tool install` / PyPI) |
````

````text
42: 
43: def _kebab(name: str) -> str:

52:         capture_output=True,
53:         text=True,
54:         env=env,
55:         check=False,

57:     if proc.returncode != 0:

59:         print(proc.stderr, file=sys.stderr)
60:         raise SystemExit(3)

88:             file=sys.stderr,

92:     _, _, tail = rest.partition(END)
````

````text
165: ## Workflow B — modernize an existing project
166: 
167: ### 1. Audit, read-only

180:   installs a default stderr sink at import. This is the most common loguru bug.

190: ### 3. One rung per pull request
191: 
192: The ladder is ordered by dependency: environment → layout → dependency
193: declaration → lint/format → types → tests → task runner + CI → console script
194: → logging layering → agent contract → secrets. Each rung ends with the test
195: suite green.
196: 
197: Read [`references/legacy-refactor.md`](references/legacy-refactor.md) before
198: the first rung. The traps that ruin these migrations — `uv add -r
199: requirements.txt` flattening the dependency graph, a formatting commit
200: destroying `git blame`, a tracked `.env` needing rotation before any history
201: rewrite — are all there.
202: 
203: ## Available scripts
204: 
205: - **`scripts/new-python-project.py <target-dir>`** — scaffold from the bundled
206:   template tree. Offline; writes nothing outside the target.
207:   - Flags: `--profile {minimal,cli,lib,api,ml,rust}`, `--name`, `--description`,
208:     `--author`, `--owner`, `--python-floor`, `--python-pin`, `--dry-run`,
209:     `--force`, `--no-git`, `--help`.
210:   - Output: JSON on stdout, progress on stderr.

213: - **`scripts/audit-python-project.py [path]`** — read-only scorecard +
214:   migration plan.
215:   - Flags: `--format {json,table}`, `--fail-on {fail,warn,never}`, `--help`.
216:   - Exit: `0` clean · `3` path is not a directory · `4` findings at or above
217:     the threshold.
218: 
219: Both are PEP 723 `uv run` scripts with inline dependencies — no environment
220: setup needed before calling them.
221: 
222: ## Bundled assets
223: 
224: - `assets/project/` — the template tree. Every file ends `.tmpl`; the generator
225:   strips the suffix, substitutes placeholders, and drops
226:   `# __IF:profile,...__ … # __END__` blocks that the chosen profile does not
227:   want.
228: - `assets/manifest.toml` — maps each destination path to the profiles that get
229:   it. **A file not listed here is never copied**, and the generator fails
230:   (exit 4) if the manifest and the tree disagree in either direction.

248: ## Gotchas
249: 
250: - **`uv sync` deletes what is not in the lock.** A manual `uv pip install`
251:   disappears on the next sync with no warning. Change dependencies with
252:   `uv add` / `uv remove` so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` move together.
253: - **Do not run black and `ruff format` together.** `ruff format` is a black
254:   reimplementation; two formatters fight over magic trailing commas and quoting
255:   and every commit reformats the last one's output. Pick ruff.
256: - **A flat layout imports your source directory, not the installed package.**
257:   Missing `__init__.py`, missing `py.typed`, unshipped package data — all pass
258:   the test suite and break the user's install. `src/` is what closes that gap.
259: - **`[dependency-groups]` is not `[project.optional-dependencies]`.** An extra
260:   is published and installable by your users; a PEP 735 group is local-only.
261:   Your test runner in an extra is a defect you cannot remove without a release.
262:   `uv sync` installs the `dev` group by default.
263: - **`uv.lock` does not constrain your users — `[project.dependencies]` and
264:   `requires-python` do.** Installed as a dependency or via `uv tool install`,
265:   your package is resolved from `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` is ignored.
266:   Commit `uv.lock` to pin *your* dev and CI environment, but keep
267:   `[project.dependencies]` floors as wide as your actual API usage allows (`>=`
268:   the lowest compatible release, no `<` or `~=` upper caps).
269: - **`uv init` and `uv add` over-constrain packages by default.** `uv init` sets
270:   `requires-python` to whatever interpreter you ran it with (e.g. `>=3.13`), and
271:   `uv add foo` writes `foo>=<version-released-today>`. If others install your
272:   package, both cause avoidable solver conflicts: lower `requires-python` to the
273:   oldest non-EOL Python your features actually need (`>=3.11`), and relax
274:   `[project.dependencies]` floors after `uv add`.
275: - **`.python-version` is read by pyenv as well as uv.** A stale value silently
276:   changes which interpreter builds the venv. Write it with `uv python pin`.
277:   Use it for your preferred local interpreter (to reuse your local `uv` wheel
278:   cache); keep `requires-python` lower for consumer compatibility, and test both
279:   ends in CI. If either is on EOL Python (`<=3.10`), upgrade with `uv python pin
280:   3.13`, set `requires-python = ">=3.11"` + `ruff.target-version = "py311"`, and
281:   run `uv run ruff check --select UP --fix`.
282: - **`ruff`'s `target-version` should be your `requires-python` floor**, not
283:   your dev pin, or `UP` rewrites code to syntax your declared floor cannot run.
284: - **direnv cannot change `PS1`.** There is no `(.venv)` prompt even when the
285:   env is active — check `which python`, not the prompt. And `.envrc` needs
286:   `direnv allow` after every edit.
287: - **Tyro already has shell completion.** Do not add shtab, argcomplete, or a
288:   `completion` subcommand: `my-tool --tyro-write-completion zsh <path>`.
289:   `--tyro-print-completion` is deprecated (a stray `print()` corrupts it), the
290:   bash completion filename must equal the command name, and no package manager
291:   installs completions for you.
292: - **No `[project.scripts]` means `uv tool install` gives the user no command.**
````
